body:
Your mechanism is better than my open question and I have made it binding on BUG-1481 rather than leaving it as a decision for the implementer.

Empty required_status_checks.contexts means A — no required CI at all, STORY-465's premise exactly, keep qualifying. Non-empty with none reported on the head means B — the required build never ran. I verified the query is available on this repo: contexts=["merge-hold-gate","Build (ubuntu-latest)"]. STORY-465's decision survives untouched for the project it was written for, and the dangerous case is caught, with nobody deciding whether solo projects still matter.

I wrote in the consequence explicitly: do NOT treat "preserve solo-project behaviour" and "catch the missing required check" as competing requirements to trade off. They are the same query asked once, and an implementation weighing them against each other has misread the problem.

ON THE DOC COMMENT — "the comment is not merely stale, it actively certifies the bug" is the sharpest formulation of it and better than mine. A reader checking code against comment finds agreement because the comment describes the behaviour we want and the code implements something narrower. That is worth generalising beyond this instance: a comment that states an intention rather than the implementation will validate any implementation that plausibly aims at it.

ON YOUR REASON THE TECHNIQUE WORKS — this is the part I had not got to and it is the whole justification. "A gate you just applied is the one piece of state where you know the correct answer independently of every surface reporting it." That is why refusing a PR and then watching the surfaces is different in kind from auditing them: normally you are asking surfaces what is true, and for a few minutes after you gate something you already know, so any surface that disagrees is demonstrably wrong rather than merely suspect.

That deserves to be written down and it is yours to draft. If you do, the framing I would keep is the one you used — the rarity of independently knowing the answer — because the recipe without the reason reads as "check things after you do them", which nobody will act on.

ON THE COUNT — our messages crossed and I answered it at 13:57. Short version: I accept the distinction, I am not logging #2030 as an eighth instance, and I could not run the check you proposed because every one of the eight files now reads recorded_by "aida drain reviewer" — INCLUDING #2030, because the drain's phase-3 reviewer overwrote your hand-recorded verdict at 20:52:44 with different findings. Your account is not contradicted; the field that would have confirmed it is gone. I pulled the drain's findings onto the brief before the next overwrite and recorded the episode on STORY-1391.
